requirement_structuring.structuring_summary: The requirement describes the capability of a routing switch to filter traffic. The lexical ambiguity regarding the direction of filtering (allow vs. block) is resolved using the glossary definition which defines 'filter' as 'Inspect and drop packets'. The supported interpretation is that the switch has the capability to selectively block specific traffic.

source_fragments: Routing switches ability to filter network traffic between data-plane interfaces and management data traffic.

fields.condition: When operating within an industrial railway communication network
fields.object: network traffic between data-plane interfaces and management data traffic

structured_requirements.final_statement: The routing switch shall have the capability to selectively block specific network traffic while allowing others between data-plane interfaces and management data traffic.
structuring_notes: The term 'filter' was lexically ambiguous but resolved via the glossary definition ('Inspect and drop packets').
The supported interpretation aligns with the definition of 'drop' as the primary action of filtering in this context.

preserved_uncertainties: The specific criteria for determining which traffic to block (e.g., specific protocols or ports beyond the general definition) are not explicitly detailed in the requirement text, though the glossary provides the mechanism.
unsupported_inferences_avoided: No external knowledge or invented actors, business rules, or metrics were used.
